question.problem:
$$
r(x,\theta )=⟨x,\,\operatorname{tan}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\text{_______}⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $r(x,\theta )$ above parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis for $x\in [0,\frac{\pi }{4}].$ What is the third component of $r?$

current_example.problem: The vector-valued function $\mathbf{r}(x,\theta)$ parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $y=x^2$ by $2\pi$ radians about the $x$-axis for $x \in \left[0, 1\right].$ What is $\mathbf{r}?$
current_example.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14275690/assets/56a380b075d10862170ed9c9a45c07dddff3eaef1ea9fb3109a61cc3d27b5ac4.png)

 

A point $(x,y,z)$ on the surface generated by rotating the graph of $y=f(x)$ by $2\pi$ radians about the $x$-axis for $x\in[a,b]$ has the position vector

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨x,\,f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,x\in [a,b],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that $y=f(x) = x^2 \geq 0$ for all $x \in \left[0,1\right].$

So, the parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
\mathbf{r}(x,\theta) = \big\langle x, \: x^2 \cos\theta, \: x^2\sin\theta \big\rangle,
\quad
x \in \left[0, 1\right],
\quad
\theta \in [0,2\pi).
$$
